key_insight: A linear eddy-viscosity closure can stabilize the ensemble-averaged adjoint equations, revealing a universal wall-shear sensitivity field whose growth is governed by chaotic backward-time dynamics and structured by Orr-type and streak-like components.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more reliable way to infer past turbulence states from wall measurements, which is useful for sensing, estimation, and control in wall-bounded flows.
method: Solve the adjoint Navier–Stokes equations backward in time from a wall-sensor kernel.
Add a linear eddy-viscosity closure to the ensemble-averaged adjoint equations to suppress chaotic energy growth.
Compare predicted mean domain of dependence (DOD) with direct ensemble averaging and contrast it with the actuator domain of influence (DOI).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct computation of the mean DOD and comparison against ensemble averages, along with cross-Reynolds-number behavior for wall-stress DOD/DOI.
watch_item: The closure is applied to the ensemble-averaged adjoint field, so single-realization chaos and qualitative structure differences may still limit pointwise prediction accuracy.
paper_title: Mitigating adjoint chaos in wall turbulence
